ref_extractions.title: Dataset of human medial temporal lobe neurons, scalp and intracranial EEG during a verbal working memory task
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This is the original dataset descriptor for data collected at University Hospital Zurich using the modified Sternberg WM task. However it describes only 9 subjects with different sampling rates (200 Hz scalp, 2 kHz iEEG), whereas the target dataset has 15 subjects at 2000 Hz. This appears to be a precursor or related subset. It defines the task paradigm and data structure but does not explicitly describe using the openneuro_ds004752 dataset.
ref_extractions.epoch_params: encoding 2s, maintenance 3s, segmentation by trial phase
ref_extractions.super_meta_note: Contains per-trial metadata including set size, match/mismatch, response correctness, RT. Original publication of the data collection protocol used by the same lab.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Describes 9 subjects performing modified Sternberg task with encoding/maintenance/recall phases, with detailed trial-level metadata. Sampling at 200 Hz (scalp) and 2 kHz (iEEG). Provides spike sorting metrics and electrode localization.

ref_extractions.title: Information flows from hippocampus to auditory cortex during replay of verbal working memory items
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper explicitly uses the openneuro_ds004752 dataset, as it references analyzing 'directed functional coupling between hippocampal LFP and the beamforming sources of scalp EEG in all 15 participants' - matching the dataset's 15 subjects. It applies Granger causality to analyze information flow during the same modified Sternberg WM task.
ref_extractions.epoch_params: encoding 2s, maintenance 3s, [4 8] Hz theta band analysis
ref_extractions.super_meta_note: Analyzes information flow direction (Granger causality) as continuous measure. Uses beamforming sources from scalp EEG and hippocampal LFP simultaneously.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: 15 participants, 71 sessions, modified Sternberg task (4/6/8 letters). Analyzes theta-band [4-8 Hz] Granger causality between hippocampus and auditory cortex during encoding and maintenance.

ref_extractions.title: Dataset of human medial temporal lobe neurons, scalp and intracranial EEG during a verbal working memory task
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This is the PDF version of the Scientific Data descriptor (same DOI as file 1). It describes the original data collection from 9 subjects with detailed methodology. While it defines the dataset structure, it describes only 9 subjects at different sampling rates than the target dataset's 15 subjects at 2000 Hz.
ref_extractions.super_meta_note: Original dataset descriptor providing per-trial metadata and electrode localization information. Detailed spike sorting quality metrics provided.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Full PDF of dataset descriptor with methods: 9 subjects, depth electrodes in hippocampus/entorhinal/amygdala, microelectrodes for single-unit recording, scalp EEG 10-20 system.

ref_extractions.title: Neural Dynamics of Visual Stream Interactions During Memory-Guided Actions Investigated by Intracranial EEG
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper investigates dorsal/ventral visual stream interactions during a delayed action task with object identity and location memory - a different paradigm from the verbal Sternberg WM task. While it involves iEEG in epilepsy patients, it does not use the openneuro_ds004752 dataset or the verbal working memory paradigm.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Different task paradigm: delayed action with object identity/location memory using joystick response. Analyzes alpha/theta oscillations in dorsal stream (IPL) and ventral stream (VTC) and hippocampus.

ref_extractions.title: Re-evaluating human MTL in working memory: insights from intracranial recordings
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This is a review paper synthesizing findings from multiple intracranial recording studies about MTL involvement in WM. It does not present new experimental data or use any specific dataset. While it references some of the same research group's work, it is a literature review rather than a study using the target dataset.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Review paper summarizing MTL contributions to WM from intracranial recordings. Cites Boran et al. 2019 and other studies but does not use the dataset directly.

ref_extractions.title: Functional specialization and interaction in the amygdala-hippocampus circuit during working memory processing
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper uses a modified Sternberg WM task (4/6/8 letters) with 14 epilepsy patients and records from amygdala and hippocampus. While it uses a very similar paradigm, it reports 14 subjects (not 15) and the dataset is likely from the same lab but may be a different collection. It uses representational analysis and machine learning but does not explicitly reference openneuro_ds004752.
ref_extractions.super_meta_note: Uses representational similarity analysis (RSA) and machine learning to classify WM load from neural patterns. Bidirectional information flow analysis.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: 14 patients (7 female), 65 sessions. Records iEEG from amygdala and hippocampus. Uses multivariate RSA, information flow (Granger causality), and neural pattern classification.

ref_extractions.title: Enhanced role of the entorhinal cortex in adapting to increased working memory load
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper uses a modified Sternberg WM task with 13 epilepsy patients, recording iEEG from entorhinal cortex, hippocampus, and lateral temporal cortex. Uses SVM to decode WM load. While it uses the same lab's paradigm, it reports 13 subjects (not 15) and does not explicitly cite openneuro_ds004752.
ref_extractions.super_meta_note: Uses multivariate SVM decoding of WM load from power features. Cross-regional decoding generalization analysis. Load-dependent connectivity analysis.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: 13 patients (6 female). Decodes load 4 vs 6 and load 6 vs 8 separately. Records from EC, hippocampus, LTC. Phase synchronization analysis.

ref_extractions.title: Human hippocampal reactivation of amygdala encoding-related gamma patterns during aversive memory retrieval
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper studies emotional episodic memory encoding and retrieval of aversive/neutral scenes, not verbal working memory. It uses a different paradigm (scene viewing with remember/familiar/new responses) and different brain structures. Does not use the openneuro_ds004752 dataset.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: 23 participants, scene encoding (0.5s) and recognition 24h later. Records amygdala and hippocampus iEEG. Analyzes gamma activity and representational similarity for emotional vs neutral stimuli.

feasibility_reason: Although the BIDS events.tsv lacks trial-level markers, multiple relevant and partial references confirm this is a well-documented modified Sternberg verbal WM dataset with clear encoding/maintenance/recall phases that supports regression (Granger causality, information flow) and classification (load decoding) tasks. The behavioral/trial structure is documented in the references and accompanying materials.
tasks_section:
## Tasks

### Classical Task 1: Working Memory Load Classification
- **Task Type**: classification
- **Epoch Method**: `epoch_by_event_hdf5`
- **Epoch Parameters**: tmin=-0.5, tmax=3.0, baseline=(None), event_id=`stimulus_onset`
- **Label Route**: `misc`
- **Meta Level**: `super`
- **Target Definition**:

| Event | y | Meaning |
|-------|---|---------|
| stimulus_onset | 4 | Set size = 4 items (low load) |
| stimulus_onset | 6 | Set size = 6 items (medium load) |
| stimulus_onset | 8 | Set size = 8 items (high load) |

- **Evidence**: [10.7554/eLife.78677](https://doi.org/10.7554/eLife.78677) | [10.1038/s41467-023-38571-w](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-023-38571-w) | [10.1038/s41467-025-60681-w](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-60681-w)
- **Kernel Notes**: Three-class WM load classification (4 vs 6 vs 8 items). Requires parsing trial metadata from accompanying behavioral logs to extract set_size per trial. SVM decoding and RSA approaches documented in references. Focus on encoding and early maintenance phases where load effects are strongest. Theta-band [4-8 Hz] activity particularly informative for MTL structures.

### Classical Task 2: Theta-Band Connectivity Analysis
- **Task Type**: regression
- **Epoch Method**: `epoch_by_event_hdf5`
- **Epoch Parameters**: tmin=-0.5, tmax=3.0, baseline=(None), event_id=`stimulus_onset`
- **Label Route**: `event`
- **Meta Level**: `super`
- **Target Definition**:

| Event | y | Meaning |
|-------|---|---------|
| stimulus_onset | continuous | Granger causality direction (hippocampus→cortex vs cortex→hippocampus) |

- **Evidence**: [10.7554/eLife.78677](https://doi.org/10.7554/eLife.78677)
- **Kernel Notes**: Directional information flow analysis [4-8 Hz] between hippocampus and auditory cortex. Requires beamformer source reconstruction and pairwise Granger causality estimation. Reversal of flow direction between encoding (auditory→hippocampus) and maintenance (hippocampus→auditory) phases documented. 15 subjects, 71 sessions, 50 trials each.

### Potential Task 1: Continuous Segmentation for Memory Phase Analysis
- **Task Type**: regression
- **Epoch Method**: `epoch_by_segmentation_hdf5`
- **Epoch Parameters**: segment_length=2.0, overlap=0.5
- **Label Route**: `event`
- **Meta Level**: `raw`
- **Target Definition**: None (no event tags in BIDS events.tsv; behavioral phase timing unavailable)
- **Evidence**: [10.1038/s41597-020-0364-3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-020-0364-3)
- **Kernel Notes**: Sternberg task has encoding (2s) → maintenance (3s) → recall phases. Continuous segmentation recommended when trial events not accessible from events.tsv. Requires downsampling from 2000 Hz to ~500 Hz before analysis. Epilepsy patients: exclude ictal segments using amplitude threshold.

### Normal Task 1: Response Correctness Classification
- **Task Type**: classification
- **Epoch Method**: `epoch_by_event_hdf5`
- **Epoch Parameters**: tmin=-0.5, tmax=1.5, baseline=(None), event_id=`response`
- **Label Route**: `misc`
- **Meta Level**: `super`
- **Target Definition**:

| Event | y | Meaning |
|-------|---|---------|
| response | 1 | Correct recall |
| response | 0 | Incorrect recall |

- **Evidence**: [10.1038/s41597-020-0364-3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-020-0364-3) | [10.7554/eLife.78677](https://doi.org/10.7554/eLife.78677)
- **Kernel Notes**: Binary correct/incorrect classification using response event timing. Requires behavioral logs for correctness labels. Imbalanced classes expected (high accuracy typical in Sternberg task). Post-response analysis to identify error-related neural signatures.

### Normal Task 2: Match/Mismatch Classification
- **Task Type**: classification
- **Epoch Method**: `epoch_by_event_hdf5`
- **Epoch Parameters**: tmin=-0.5, tmax=2.0, baseline=(None), event_id=`probe_onset`
- **Label Route**: `misc`
- **Meta Level**: `super`
- **Target Definition**:

| Event | y | Meaning |
|-------|---|---------|
| probe_onset | 1 | Probe matches encoded set |
| probe_onset | 0 | Probe does not match encoded set |

- **Evidence**: [10.1038/s41597-020-0364-3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-020-0364-3)
- **Kernel Notes**: Probe-locked epochs to analyze recognition memory processes. Match trials require maintenance of items in WM; mismatch trials require comparison. Event_id `probe_onset` referenced in original publications but must be verified in actual BIDS structure. Requires behavioral logs for trial type labels.

### Potential Task 2: Single-Unit Spike Pattern Analysis
- **Task Type**: classification
- **Epoch Method**: `epoch_by_event_hdf5`
- **Epoch Parameters**: tmin=-1.0, tmax=3.0, baseline=(None), event_id=`stimulus_onset`
- **Label Route**: `misc`
- **Meta Level**: `super`
- **Target Definition**:

| Event | y | Meaning |
|-------|---|---------|
| stimulus_onset | spike_pattern_id | Multi-unit spike pattern type |

- **Evidence**: [10.1038/s41597-020-0364-3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-020-0364-3)
- **Kernel Notes**: Dataset includes single-unit neuron spike times from microelectrodes in MTL structures (hippocampus, entorhinal cortex, amygdala). Requires synchronizing spike times with stimulus events. Spike sorting quality metrics available in dataset descriptor. Plausibly supports cell assembly pattern classification during encoding.
